name: Meta Infotech Ltd
title: Meta Infotech Ltd - 544441 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: H1 FY27 revenue fell 57% YoY to INR89.5 crore as Meta exited low-margin product sales to one bank; EBITDA margin rose to 8.7%.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was INR89.5 crore in H1 FY27 versus INR210 crore in H1 FY26, down 57% YoY, which management attributed to deliberately discontinuing lower-margin product sales to one leading bank. Sequentially, revenue rose 49% from INR59.9 crore in H2 FY26. EBITDA was INR7.8 crore (8.7% margin) versus INR15.8 crore (7.5%) a year earlier and INR2.3 crore (3.8%) in H2 FY26. PAT was INR4.9 crore versus INR10.4 crore in H1 FY26, with the order book at INR92.7 crore as of September 2026.

segments.name: Services (incl. managed/sustenance)
segments.commentary: Services mix rose to about 71% from about 15% historically; management says recurring sustenance/managed services stand at INR21.5 crore, with 30+ customers on contracts of more than five years. Contracts are renewed with 8-10% annual increases.

segments.name: Product sales
segments.commentary: Product share fell to about 29% from about 85%. Lower-margin product sales to one bank were discontinued, though the services relationship with that client continues.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated a FY29 target of 4x PAT versus FY26 and said it is on track.
Expects PAT growth of 30%+ year-on-year, rising in later years, though it declined to give numbers.
Targets net profit from recurring business covering about 50% of costs this year, 75% next, and 100% within two years.
Plans to add 50-70% YoY to recurring business; new business of INR20-30 crore per year is expected.
Management said it is not focused on top-line growth for now and is prioritising gross profit and PAT.
Working toward signing one of the largest US system integrators; identifying global partners for services-only engagements.
capex_capacity: Expanded from one location (Mumbai) to five Indian locations (Mumbai, Bangalore, Chennai, Hyderabad, Delhi) plus six Gulf locations.
Vendor base increased by about 10 (eight added per one remark; three onboarded in H1 FY27 per the prepared remarks).
Targets 50 top accounts in Mumbai (expected to yield about 80% of business) and 15 accounts each in Bangalore, Chennai, Hyderabad and Delhi.
Management says the foundation and shift are complete, with H2 expected to show greater vendor and business engagement.
demand_pricing: Added 12 new clients in H1 FY27 across sectors and geographies.
Management says AI adoption is increasing cybersecurity demand; AI security is an add-on offering, and no AI security deal has been closed yet although several are in progress.
Management claims little competition in managed services, citing IBM and Wipro as failing on quality in large-bank sustenance work.
Remains in niche cybersecurity; does not sell firewalls or software and does not focus on one-time consulting.

qa_highlights.question: What are the key growth drivers for the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited new locations, vendor additions and a shift to services; it said the foundation is built and recurring sustenance revenue should grow 50-70% a year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company on track for FY29 4x PAT versus FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 4x PAT is the ultimate target and it is on track, supported by recurring business and new business of INR20-30 crore a year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the contribution of top clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not comment on the top five clients. It said one client previously made up 30-45% of revenue and it is moving away from concentration.

qa_highlights.question: How are new regions contributing to top line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not focused on top line and that product revenue will drive it; regional contribution was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: How is Meta positioned for AI-related security demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI increases cybersecurity demand; AI security is an additional offering and no AI security deal has been closed yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for revenue growth over the next quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management focused on PAT, guiding to 30%+ YoY PAT growth, and said the new vendors and locations need to generate revenue.

risks_watch: Revenue decline of 57% YoY; order book of INR92.7 crore is below historical levels, so conversion into revenue must be tracked.
Dependence on sustenance/managed services for recurring income; the INR21.5 crore base must grow as guided.
Execution across five Indian and six Gulf locations, and the ramp of about 10 new vendors.
Management declined to give quantified guidance (for example, PAT growth in exact terms), so targets are not verifiable yet.
Client concentration history: one client previously accounted for 30-45% of revenue.
Pending signing with a large US system integrator is not yet closed.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on the services transition and the 4x PAT target, but evasive on quantified numbers (top-five client share, top-line, PAT growth), citing compliance. Management acknowledged the weak revenue prints and asked investors to wait for H2 results.
key_quotes: We consciously decided to discontinue certain lower-margin product sales to a leading bank, one particular bank, as part of our strategy to focus on higher-value cybersecurity services.
But we are done with creating the foundation and the shift with H1.
We're not looking at Top 5 because it's too risky and putting all the eggs in five customers will be risky.
Cybersecurity is one of the industries which will never be affected by negative effect of AI.

adds.what: Expansion from Mumbai to five Indian locations (Mumbai, Bangalore, Chennai, Hyderabad, Delhi) plus six Gulf locations; footprint expansion, no capex figure give

growth.why: Management guides PAT growth of 30%+ YoY and a FY29 target of 4x FY26 PAT, with no revenue guidance and explicit de-emphasis of top-line growth; backing is partial (recurring base of INR21.5 cr with 8-10% escalators, about INR7 cr/yr added, 12 new clients, INR92.7 cr order book described as below history) and no AI security deal closed yet.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose to 8.7% in H1 FY27 from 3.8% in H2 FY26 as services mix rose to 71% from about 15%, and management targets recurring business covering 50% of costs this year, 75% next, and 100% within two years.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Footprint already expanded from Mumbai to five Indian and six Gulf locations, and management says the foundation and shift are complete, with H2 engagement expected; no utilisation or capex figure was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides recurring sustenance revenue up 50-70% YoY from INR21.5 crore, with INR20-30 crore of new business a year and 12 new clients added in H1 FY27, though H1 revenue fell 57% YoY to INR89.5 crore and the order book is below historical levels at INR92.7 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex figure or new plant plan was discussed, and utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no quantified revenue guidance and said it is not focused on top-line growth, so an upgrade is not signalled; it guides only to 30%+ YoY PAT growth, which it declined to quantify.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Revenue fell 57% YoY and the order book at INR92.7 crore is below historical levels, while the INR21.5 crore recurring base must grow about INR7 crore a year and the US system integrator signing is not closed.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: AI security is an add-on offering with several deals in progress but none closed yet, so a launch-linked win is conditional and no date was given.

rows.label: FY29 4x PAT target versus FY26
rows.why: Management reiterated the 4x FY26 PAT target as on track, but H1 FY27 PAT of INR4.9 crore is well below H1 FY26's INR10.4 crore, so the ramp needs a sharp H2 recovery.

rows.label: Large US system integrator signing
rows.why: Management is working toward signing one of the largest US system integrators and identifying global partners for services-only engagements, but the deal is not yet closed and no date was given.

rows.label: Recurring contract escalators
rows.why: Contracts renew with 8-10% annual increases across 30+ customers on contracts of more than five years, supporting the recurring base of INR21.5 crore.

tone.note: Management was confident on the services transition, recurring base and 4x PAT target, but evasive on quantified figures such as top-five client share, top-line and PAT growth; the Q&A probed revenue decline and the lack of numbers.

oneOffs.what: Deliberate exit from lower-margin product sales to one bank drove the 57% YoY revenue decline in H1 FY27 (INR89.5 crore vs INR210 crore); this depresses reported growth, not a one-time gain or loss

quality.why: Revenue fell 57% YoY to INR89.5 crore because Meta deliberately exited low-margin bank product sales, while mix shifted to services (71% vs about 15% historically) and EBITDA margin rose to 8.7% from 7.5%; the brief gives no volume figure and no explicit one-time gain or loss, and the H1 sequential rise of 49% QoQ is not explained as a one-off.
